← Back to Miscellaneous Home ROMANIA OSP-1948 MINISHEETS USED AS PROPAGANDA TOOLS (revisited seventy years later) Victor Manta, PWO Introduction Being in Romania, at the early age when I started collecting Romanian stamps, this set was already slightly over ten years old. I saw the set of six stamps many times, at different collectors, but I could see the whole set of six minisheets maybe two times in over 25 years. Even if the OSP minisheets were quite attractive, they were ways too expensive for me. Later I switched to collecting foreign topical stamps, that looked more interesting and were better printed, so that I forgot about these stamps. Only recently my interest in them has increased again for the reasons outlined in this article. About the OSP and related stamps series Any stamp collector with some experience in Romanian postage stamps knows the OSP (Organizaţia Sportului Popular - People's Sport Organization) issues, because some of them are rather scarce, but not everyone knows what this organization represented in the now deep past. Here is what I could find on the Web: "By establishing the People's Sport Organization (decree-law of March 7, 1946) the mass sports movement was organized and subordinated to the central policy of the PCR (Romanian Communist Party). The foundations of a seemingly harmless organization were laid, but behind the development of physical education and sport was the Communists' interest in framing society in many mass organizations to subordinate the individual to the totalitarian state." Source (in Romanian). I found out also that only a day passed between the establishment of the "first democratic government", named the government Petru Groza, and the beginning of sovietization, which was well prepared in advance. Because the new organization was thought as an another propaganda tool for the establishment of communism in Romania, on September 1, 1946, the Romanian postal service issued a set of seven values ​​(Mi. 1000-1006) and a minisheet composed of four sheets, that were cut off with scissors (Mi. Block 33). The new sport organization needed funds, which is why the stamps, as well as the sheets, were sold at a massive surcharge (Lei 160 + 1340, 300 + 1200, 300 + 1000). A new set, printed in minisheets of nine, accompanied by another sheet, followed in 1946, Scott B 279 – B 289. Two years later, in 1948, a new and last set of 6 stamps was issued, in minisheets of four, Michel 1171 - 1176. These minisheets, reproduced throughout this article, are its main subject. Scarcity There are several reasons why these minisheets are scarce: - They were issued three years after the ending of WW2, a war that devastated Romania. After the war, even if becoming an ally of the USSR and fighting against the Nazi Germany, Romania was occupied (between 1944 - 1958) by the Soviet Union, that sucked a lot from country's resources, considered them as after the war compensations. Therefore, people were too poor to buy stamps when so many more important things (like food) were missing. - The stamps were expensive, displaying a surcharge of 100 percent each. - The stamps from most of minisheets were separated from each other to be sold independently, for a quarter of the price of the sheets, what obviously made them more affordable. The separated stamps were postally valid. - The topic itself is an attractive one and it was popular especially among young people. As a result, only a small number of minisheets survived, what made them very fast scarce. It is difficult to estimate how many full minisheets escaped but their quantity is surely very limited. The catalogue and eBay prices of the OSP 1948 minisheets today Excepting for the Scott catalogue, I learned the prices for MNH stamps on the eBay, as follows: - Michel Europa 2017 - 2018, 1171 – 1176, in minisheets, MNH Euro 400 (USD 450). - Yvert & Tellier, MNH price in Euro, converted to US$: 400. - Scott, B 241 – B 424, CB 20 – CB 21, US$ 48.50 for a set. No separate prices for minisheets, that should be priced at over US$ 200. The eBay “Buy It Now” prices are varying, at the time of writing of this article, between US$ 247 and US$ 495 (!?). I can remember that a few years ago one set of minisheets was sold in an eBay-auction at US$ 217. Images & Watermarks The full set consists of three perforate and three imperforate stamps. Each minisheet contains four stamps. The imperforate stamps have the same design as the perforate ones, but their colors were changed. Only one of the stamps shows a somehow popular sport in Romania, displaying running athletes. The second one features plane modelling, a less popular sport, and the third a parade of athletes, being an obvious propaganda stamp. Therefore, the whole it is not just another trivial issue dedicated to some more or less popular sports but a propaganda tool of the freshly installed communist regime. It will reign over Romania for 45 years and it will be overturned by a popular uprising in December 1989. Watermark: Scott # 289, “RPR Multiple”. RPR, the abbreviation of “Republica Populară Română”, means the then new name given to the country, the Romanian Popular Republic. The first and the last two stamps are known with an watermark rotated by 180 degrees. The third and the fourth can be found with a reverse watermark. Created: Nov. 29, 2018. Revised: June 8, 2020. ← Back to Miscellaneous Home Sport on Romanian Stamps The sporting activity has a long tradition in Romania and this tradition was illustrated by many issues, dedicated to different sportive disciplines. We will limit ourselves to some of exceptional results of Romanian sport people during the last decades. The most outstanding Romanian sportive personality was without doubt Nadia Comaneci , the revelation of the Olympic Games in Montreal, 1976, and the first gymnast to be recompensed by the maximal notes by all judges in a competition of a highest level. The sheet displayed below, issued shortly after the Olympic games from Montreal, was dedicated to her, even if an anonymous person is shown. The success of Nadia Comaneci was the coronation of a long series of excellent results of Romanian sportsmen at Olympic Games, as shown by a later sheet, issued in 1984, and dedicated to the 20 gold, 16 silver and 17 bronze medals won in Los Angeles. The Romanian male players dominated during two decades the handball scene, and won four world championship titles. Players like Moser , Hnat , Stanga or Gatu were the heroes of several youth's generations, mine included. The above stamp was overprinted with the text "Romania Campioana Mondiala 1974" (World Champion). The sheet was issued in 1980 and commemorates the Romanian participation at the Olympic Games in Moscow. One of the most talented tennis players worldwide was the Romanian Ilie Nastase , the winner of many Grand Slam tournements. Together with Ion Titiac (later a very successful sportive manager) he participated three times at the final play team of the Davis Cup. The above sheet, issued in 1988, is dedicated to Grand Slam tournaments in Melbourne and Roland Garros, both won by Ilie Nastase during his glorious career. Football (soccer) was and still is the most popular sport in Romania. The communist regime forbade to most successful of Romanian player to joining of foreign clubs, and for this reason great names of the Romania football, like Ozon , Parcalab or Dobrin were less known outside Romania's borders. The most successful football team ever was that of Steaua Bucharest , that won the most prestigious of European trophies, the European Champions Cup. The Romanian national football team had excellent results in the European and World Championships, and this also thanks to its outstanding player Gheorghe Hagi . Hagi is the only sportsman whom the Romanian Post dedicated a postal issue. The sheet, issued in 2001 (above, on the left), presents the moment of Hagi's retirement from the National football team, after 17 years of loyal services. The other football stamps and the sheet on this page were issued in commemoration of the World Championship in Spain, in 1982. Created: 09/02/01. Revised: 09/10/01 . ← Back to The Country Home VILLAGE MUSEUM AND PEASANT HOUSES Rural life and civilization played a significant part in Romania's past history. In the first centuries AD, the Roman colonization had a rural character and, before the first half of the current century, most of Romania's population lived in a village environment. Farming and village communities were organized in order to cover all everyday demands. Clothes were home-made as well as different tools. The Village Museum is the major attraction of the cultural tourism in Bucharest, the capital of Romania. A creation of sociologist Dimitrie Gusti in 1936, the outdoors museum located in northern Bucharest, on the Herastrau lake shore, with verdure and lakes all around, displays, on the 30 hectares it covers 70 exhibits of households, churches and traditional techniques and devices (water and windmills, oil presses, etc) from all the country's provinces. The originality of the folk creation, the sensibility and care for the beauty of the rural people is shown in the objects found inside their households - carpets, pottery, rugs, icons, furniture. To build up the Village Museum, which Dimitrie Gusti used to call "the very chime of the Romanian nation's anonymous past", the houses were dismantled piece by piece, transported by cart, train, boat etc, and then restored in Bucharest on the Herastrau Lake bank. The oldest houses date from the 17th century, but most of them were built in the 19th century. Houses coming from hill and mountain regions are easy to identify by the raised groundwork (hosting the cellar) unlike plain field houses with their low foundation. Houses from frequently invaded regions are half-buried in the earth. Usually, slant roofs preventing snow stacks indicate northern or mountain areas. Museum's Address : 28, Kiseleff Boulevard, zip code 71 321. Telephone : +40 (1) 617 17 32, +40 (1) 617 59 29 Fax : +40 (1) 312 90 68 Visiting hours : Monday: 9:00 - 17:00, Tuesday - Sunday: 9:00 - 17:00 (Oct - May), 9:00 - 20:00 (May - Oct). The three sets shown above present peasant houses from Romania. The first set was issued on Dec.25, 1963, Scott 1590 - 1596. The second set was issued in July 21, 1986 and commemorates the 50th anniversary of the Open Air Museum of Historic Dwellings in Bucharest, Scott 3387 - 3392. The third set was issued on Feb. 8, 1989 and present the architecture of Romanian peasants houses. Please move the mouse index over the stamps for more information about the individual stamps. t: Romania as Seen through Its Stamps.
b: Over Twenty Years on the Web Discover this non-commercial site, dedicated to Romania as seen through its stamps. The site not only shows nice Romanian stamps, but tries to introduce you to this country, to its original culture, its wonderful landscapes and its friendly people. You can find here pages dedicated to Romanian history, thematic collection, postal history and to many other subjects. The site was initially thought for the beginner collectors, being enriched in time with higher-level pages describing the propaganda and commercial manipulations due to a totalitarian regime that reigned for 45 years in Romania. The site is partially bilingual English - Romanian. This site is intended for you, a person who wishes to know more about Romania. It was created and is permanently updated by Victor Manta, a Swiss stamp collector. You can benefit from his experience, because he lived many years in Romania and has a large knowledge of country's culture, language, history, literature, and also of its stamps, which he collects since childhood. A long years fan of Romanian topical stamps, he is especially interested in the relationship between the images on Romanian stamps, the tormented history of Romanian people and by the art and culture in Romania. The present site was started in 2001, when Romanian philately was virtually not present on the web. The first objective of the author was to present a large sample of Romanian postage stamps to attract as many readers as possible to their collection and presentation. This objective was largely achieved, especially after the EFIRO 2008 World Exposition, where the author presented in an exhibit all the world sites dedicated to Romanian postage stamps. Afterwards, he focused on the coverage of some special areas, sometimes very technical (like Brussels overprints), or others little covered by the philatelic press (the imperforate sheets, the Odessa massacre, cheats, forgotten champions, etc.). Many of the newer articles have been published by the author in the Romanian and international printed press. Victor Manta, a pioneer of the philatelic web, is a former member of the Association of Romanian Philatelists, of the Union of Swiss Philatelic Associations and of AIJP. In 1997 the author founded PASIC (Paintings and Arts on Stamps Internet Club), counting at time over 700 members from 70 countries, and affiliated since 1999 with the American Topical Association. This club is quite popular worldwide, and especially in Romanian philatelic circles, which is reflected by the fact that the second largest participation in PASIC comes from Romania. Mr. Victor Manta is also the founder of the Philatelic Webmasters Organization (PWO) that counts over 350 members. This organization actively fights against the proliferation of illegal and excessive stamp issues. His Arts on Stamps site, that includes a large chapter on Romanian art, partially included in this site, was internationally awarded in the year 2000. In the year 2002 at the PhilaKorea Philatelic Exhibition in Seoul this site was awarded "Three Stars" by the International Philatelic Association (FIP). In 2018 it was awarded Vermeil at the Italia 2018 International Exhibition, and in 2019 Large Vermeil at an International Exhibition in Belarus . Please use the menu displayed in the left frame to navigate this site. Thank you for your interest in the large and often so challenging Romanian philately! Romania vazuta prin timbrele ei De 20 de ani pe Web Descoperiţi acest site necomercial dedicat României, aşa cum este ea arătată de câtre timbrele pe care le-a emis. Site-ul nu numai ca vă prezintă frumoase mărci romaneşti, dar încearcă sa le facă cunoscute celor care ştiu mai puţine aceasta tară cultura ei originală, peisajele ei minunate şi oamenii ei prietenoşi. Veţi putea găsi pe acest site pagini dedicate istoriei României, mărcilor ei tematice, istoriei ei poştale si multor alte subiecte. Site-ul a fost gândit iniţial pentru colecţionarii începători, dar s-a îmbogăţit în timp cu pagini de un nivel mai ridicat, ce descriu manipulările propagandistice şi comerciale datorate unui regim totalitar ce a domnit timp de 45 de ani în Romania. Site-ul este parţial bilingv englez - român. Acest site este conceput si realizat pentru dvs., o persoana care doreşte sa afle mai multe lucruri despre România şi mărcile ei. El a fost creat şi este adus în pemanenţă la zi de catre Victor Manta, un colecţionar de marci poştale din Elveţia. Puteţi beneficia de experienţa lui, deoarece el a locuit multi ani in România şi cunoaşte bine cultura, limba , istoria şi mărcile acestei ţări, pe care le colectioneaza din copilarie. D omeniile sale de interes se refera la legaturile între imaginile arătate pe timbrele romaneşti şi istoria frământata a poporului roman, precum şi la arta romaneasca, cărora le consacră un numar important de pagini. Site-ul prezent a fost creat în anul 2001, atunci când filatelia românească nu era practic prezentă pe web. Primul obiectiv al autorului a fost să publice un extras cât mai larg din emisiunile de mărci poştale româneşti, pentru a atrage cât mai mulţi cititori către colecţionarea şi prezentarea acestora. Acest obiectiv a fost în bună măsură atins, în special după expoziţia mondială EFIRO 2008, unde autorul a prezentat într-un exponat toate site-urile mondiale consacrate mărcilor poştale româneşti. După aceea el s-a concentrat pe acoperirea unor domenii speciale, uneori foarte tehnice (precu supratiparele Bruxelles), alteori puţin acoperite de presa filatelică (coliţele nedantelate, masacrul din Odesa, trişări, campioni sortiţi uitării, etc.). Multe dintre articolele mai noi au fost publicate de autor şi în presa scrisă românească şi internaţională. Victor Manta este un fost membru al Asociatiei Filateliştilor Români, al Uniunii Asociatiilor Filatelice Elvetiene şi al lui AIJP (Asociaţia Internaţională a Jurnaliştilor Filatelici). În 1997 el a fondat PASIC (Paintings and Arts on Stamps Internet Club), care numără peste 800 de membri din 80 de ţări, club care este afiliat din 1999 la American Topical Association (Asociaţia Americană a Colecţionarilor Tematici). El este de asemeni fondatorul si Presedintele lui Philatelic Webmasters Organization (Organizatia Webmasterilor Filatelici) , cu peste 350 de membri . Această organizaţie luptă activ împotriva proliferării timbrelor poştale ilegale şi excesive. Site-ul creat de Dl . Manta , intitulat Arts on Stamps (Arta pe timbre), a fost recompensat cu multe premii de prestigiu , printre care şi cel al FIP (Federatia Internationala de Filatelie). De menţionat că unele pagini ale acestui site, referitoare la pictură, au fost preluate de pe site-ul citat înainte. În anul 2002 prezentul site a fost premiat de catre Federaţia Internationala de Filatelie, in cadrul expozitiei mondiale PhilaKorea in Seul. În noiembrie 2018 acest site a fost premiat cu medalia Vermeil la Italia 2018 International Exhibition, iar in 2019 a primit recompensa Large Vermeil în Bielorusia, la expozitia Belphila 2019. ← Back to The Country Home THE WATCH MUSEUM The Watch Museum , unique in Romania, was inaugurated in 1963 in a room of the Culture Palace in Pitesti. The museum exIsts thanks to professor Nicolae Simache, who was the director of the History Museum between 1954 - 1971. The watch collection was moved later in a house built at the end of the 19th century. This house belonged to the former Prefect (Governor) of the Prahova district , Luca Elefterescu, a renown conservative politician who was active at the beginning of first decade of the 20th century. The museum introduces its visitors to the domain of the evolution of means for the time measuring, from first sun watches to burning watches, watches with water and with sand till the antiques and modern ones. The wonderful works are very often not only masterpieces of renown horlogical masters, but also of artists, who contributed to their attractive presentation and created schools and styles. We display below several exhibits from the museum's collection, as shown on six postal stamps that appeared on 20th of May 1988 under the name "The Watch Museum Ploiesti". 50 B. Muzeul Ceasului, un muzeu unic România, a fost inaugurat în anul 1963, într-o sală a Palatului Culturii din Ploieşti. Muzeul îşi datorează existenţa profesorului Nicolae Simache, director al Muzeului de Istorie între anii 1954 - 1971. Colecţia de ceasuri a fost mutată ulterior într-o clădire construită la sfârşitul secolului al XIX-lea. Această clădire a aparţinut fostului prefect al judeţului Prahova, Luca Elefterescu, cunoscut politician conservator, activ în primele decenii ale secolului al XX-lea. Muzeul îşi propune să îşi introducă vizitatorii în tematica evoluţiei mijloacelor de măsurare a timpului, de la primele "ceasuri" cu cadranele solare, ceasurile arzătoare, cu apă sau cu nisip, până la ceasornicele mecanice "antice" şi cele moderne. Minunate lucrări de orologerie sunt adeseori nu numai opera unor vestiţi meşteri ceasornicari, ci şi a oamenilor de artă, care au contribuit la prezentarea lor cât mai atrăgătoare, creând adevărate stiluri. Vă prezentăm în cele ce urmează câteva capodopere din colecţia muzeului, făcând apel pentru aceasta la emisiunea de şase mărci poştale româneşti, apărută pe data de 20 mai 1988 şi intitulată "Muzeul Ceasului - Ploieşti". 50 B. ← Back to Miscellaneous Home Wildlife on Romanian Stamps Due to the variety of its relief and of the lower industrialization of certain regions, Romania still preserves a lot from its original flora and fauna. One can find here some wild beast that have disappeared in other regions of Europe. The Delta of Danube, the second biggest European river, is an unique place in what concerns the variety of its population of birds. Some Nice Flowers Discussion Q: Why have you shown the flowers? Is there anything specifically Romanian about these flowers? As I see them, these flowers grow everywhere in Europe. It would be nice if you would write something about them to indicate why they are special for your page. A: May I remind you "Le Petit Prince" by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry? The prince loved a flower, but suddenly he observed that his flower is just one among many, many others, very similar ones. Confronted with this problem, he suddenly understood that his flower is special to him because it was in his care and also because he has chosen to love this one for reason that only his heart could explain. That's maybe the explanation why the flowers of my country, flowers that I know well because I have grown among them, are nicer for me than many rare, special or exotic ones, from my country of from abroad. That should be the reason why I have chosen to show these very flowers, so nicely reproduced on the above stamps. Fauna si flora Datorita varietatii reliefului si a unui grad de industrializare mai scazut in unele regiuni, Romania reusit sa pastreze o mare parte din floara si fauna sa originala. Aici se pot intalni animale care au disparut demult in alte zone ale Europei, un loc de vis atat pentru amatorii de natura, cat si pentru pasionatii vanatorii si pescuitului. Delta Dunarii (al doilea cel mai mare rau al Europei) este un loc unic in ceea ce priveste varietatea populatiei sale de pasari. Niste flori frumoase Discutie (traducere din engleza) Intrebare : De ce ati aratat florile de pe aceasta pagina? Au ele ceva specific romanesc? Asa cum le cunosc, ele cresc aproape peste tot in Europa. Raspuns: Poti sa va reamintesc Micul Print, de Antoine de Saint-Exup�ry? Printul era indragostit de o floare, dar deodata el a observat ca aceasta este numei una dintre multe altele care cresteau in vecinatate. Confruntat cu aceasta problema, printul a inteles ca aceasta floare reprezinta ceva deosebit pentru el deoarece ea era in grija lui, si, in plus, ca el a simtit ca iubeste aceasta floare din primul moment, pentru motive pe care numei inima lui le cunostea. Aceasta ar putea sa fie explicatia de ce florile tarii mele, pe care le cunosc bine si printre care am crescut, imi par mai frumoase decat multe altele, poate mai aratoase, dar straine. Aceast trebuie sa fie motivul care m-a determinat sa aleg sa va prezint aceste flori, atat de bine reproduse pe marcile de mai sus. t: Romania in the World War I
b: ← Back to History Home ROMANIA IN THE WORLD WAR I Romania takes no part in the First Balkan War of 1912-13, fought to drive the Ottomans out of the western Balkans. In the Second Balkan War of June-July 1913 it gains Southern Dobrogea from Bulgaria. At the outset of WWI Romania remains neutral despite its alliance commitments to Austria. It joins the war on the Allied side in Aug. 27, 1916 (by declaring war on Austro-Hungary) after receiving territorial promises. On the same day the High Command Headquarters issued decree No.2798 proclaiming a state of siege. As a consequence of this, censorship procedures were established with the first day of censorship being August 27 1916. In the capital town of each county a censorship office was established by the military. All the mail from a particular county had to be censored at the capital town. German Occupation Stamps, cancelled in Bucharest in 1917 Romanian forces move into Transylvania but are driven out within two months. By Jan. 1917 German-Austrian and Bulgarian offensives have overrun most of the country Before the occupation of Bucharest, the Romanian government decided on November 12/25 1916 to move all the official institutions to Iasi which was the "historical capital" of Moldavia, in lands held by their Russian ally. Russia leaves the war early in 1918, and Romania is forced to accept the Treaty of Bucharest of May 7, 1918 that makes the country a client of Germany and Austria. Please see below a Romanian banknote issued in 1917 by the Romanian General Bank, that is "backed by a depot in cash at the Bank of the German Empire, Berlin." Romania yields control of the Carpathian passes to Austria and cedes Dobrogea and the mouths of the Danube partly to Bulgaria, partly to a condominium of Germany, Austria and Bulgaria. The Central Powers accept Romania's acquisition of Bessarabia from Russia. Please see below a German occupation stamp, 1917, and a send/replay stationary card, June 1917, both overprinted Rumänien (Romania). Romania ends the war with high casualities and little glory, but it has an intact army and no strong neighbors. It is able to acquire all of Bessarabia and the Bukovina, all of historic Transylvania with adjacent lands to the west, and most of the Banat. As a result, Romania after 1919 is twice the size of pre-war Romania. Romania's monarchic constitutional order survives the war with little immediate change. Most of Romania's borders today are those of 1919, but WWII costs it not only Bessarabia and northern Bukovina (annexed by Soviet Russia) and southern Dobrogea (restored to Bulgaria), but for 40 years also its freedom. After: http://dmorgan.web.wesleyan.edu/balkans/wwone.htm ) Because the Romanian PA hasn't issued special stamps related to the WWI during the war, we show some interesting postcards, displaying foreign soldiers and the common text: Our Allies. They were designed by Steurer. In the first row soldiers from: England, Russia (Cossack), and France. The above soldiers are from: Japan, Belgium, and Serbia. Zeppelins in Romania and Worldwide Zeppelins in Romania and Worldwide Victor Manta Introduction Zeppelins revolutionized mail delivery by transporting letters and postal materials swiftly across continents. Their speed and reliability marked a new era in intercontinental communication, allowing letters to traverse long distances in a matter of days rather than weeks. This innovation bridged geographical gaps and facilitated global connections. To send post from different countries to Friedrichshafen for delivery by zeppelins, a sender would typically follow established postal procedures. They would visit their local post office, pay the required postage, and hand over the mail to be transported. These letters and parcels would be sorted, stamped, and prepared for zeppelin transport. Fig.1. Graf Ferdinand von Zeppelin (1838 - 1917) - Postcard Upon arrival in Friedrichshafen, the mail would be received and processed by the zeppelin company's postal authorities. It would then be sorted according to its final destination. The zeppelin's onboard post office staff played a critical role in this process. Once the zeppelin reached its destination city, the mail would be handed over to the local postal authorities for final delivery to the addressees. Fig. 2. Romanian year 2000 FDC that commemorates the first zeppelin flight The above envelope, issued by the Romanian Post in 2000, commemorates 100 years since the first flight of the rigid-frame zeppelin. Zeppelins in Romania In the early 20th century, Romania also embraced the innovative method of sending letters by zeppelins. The country established zeppelin routes that connected it with other European nations, enabling efficient and expedited mail delivery. This advancement in communication technology played a crucial role in fostering international connections and trade for Romania. Fig. 4. Cover sent in Oct. 1932 by airship Graf Zeppelin from Bucharest to Buenos Aires, Argentina Fig. 5. The back side of the above cover On the envelope we see a selection of mostly high-value stamps, typical for this period, with a total face value of 102 lei. For comparison, then the average salary was around 120 lei, and a registered letter sent by plane to Argentina cost 12 lei. This made the sending price exorbitant for a typical Romanian citizen, but it was apparently within the reach of the German citizen mentioned on the back of the letter. We notice the incomplete address of the addressee, which apparently did not prevent the letter from reaching its destination. All stamps are special, not belonging to the Romanian post office. Four of them are dated October 5, 1932, and the 5th indicates the following day, when the letter possibly left for Friedrichshaven, Germany, the departure point of the airship. Another stamp attests that on November 10 the envelope arrived at the location of the airship. A blurred stamp with the inscription "Certificados ??central" suggests the certification of the shipment. The stamp on the back indicates the date of October 15, the date of the airship's arrival in Buenos Aires, so the flight lasted about six days, a good performance compared to a letter sent by plane, which then arrived in 10-15 days. Another cover, sent by the precedent flight, is presented below for comparison. Fig. 6. Cover sent on Sep. 1932 from Bucharest to Buenos Aires, Argentina The total value of the postage is 101 lei, very close to the one on the previous letter and which also corresponds very well with the company's shipping price in Reichsmark, converted at the current exchange rate. I notice that this time the letter was sent with a previous race, on September 6, 1932, and it has an image showing that it is the balloon race in the 6th trip to South America. The recipient's address appears complete, and the "MIT ZEPPELIN Europa-Südamerica" label is attractive. I also noticed that the two letters seem to be sent to the same address and are written in the same handwriting, which leads me to believe that they have the same sender (a collector, a dealer?). I find it interesting that the first envelope reached at an auction on ebay the price of US$ 329.50, while the other one was offered at a fixed price of $150 by a well-known trading house. A beautiful performance for an envelope sent from Romania! The tragic end of the zeppelins era Advancements in aviation technology, particularly the development of more efficient and safer airplanes, made zeppelins less competitive in terms of speed, cost, and reliability. The infamous Hindenburg disaster in 1937, where the German passenger airship LZ 129 Hindenburg caught fire while attempting to land, further eroded public confidence in zeppelins. Fig. 7. Burned card from disastrous flight to New York of Hindenburg zeppelin in 1937 The irresistible attraction of zeppelins New zeppelin stamps and covers collectors can start today with recent philatelic issues, such as the nice ones or similar, shown below. Fig. 8. Romanian maxxicard of 1978 Fig. 9. Romanian FDC of 1979. 50 years since the flight Sibiu - Bucharest, on Balkan route Then, depending on their financial means at their disposal, they can venture into collecting postal issues from the zeppelin era. Below, on a cover, are my US favorites stamps, issued in 1930, Scott C13-15, that were used exclusively on mail carried via Graf Zeppelin on its European – Pan American flights. Fig. 10.
